purpose: Screenshots of other products, used as the outside comparison for design review of the Clipping Factory studio.

roles.reference: A real application window captured at a native viewport size. These are the only files a comparative judge is scored against.
roles.aspiration: Vendor marketing art: cropped single surfaces, 720 to 1400 px wide, not a whole app window at a native size. Kept for looking at, never scored against.

note: Files marked role "reference" were captured from the running application on this machine, at the same CSS pixel sizes and device scale factor as the studio's own shots, so both sides of a comparison are the same kind of image. Files marked role "aspiration" are third-party marketing assets kept for internal design reference; each was published by its vendor. Do not redistribute either kind as part of the product.

files.captured_on: Mac mini (Apple M1, macOS 26.0.1), remote over ssh
files.method: Launched the installed app with --remote-debugging-port and captured its own Chromium renderer at a 1280x800 CSS viewport, device scale factor 1, through reference/capture-t3-window.mjs. This is the app's window content, not the vendor site and not a window screenshot with macOS chrome.
files.shows: The app's new-thread screen: sidebar with search and thread groups, breadcrumb header, the empty workspace headline, the composer with its model, reasoning, access and machine selectors, and the project panel on the right.
files.note: The sidebar shows the capture machine's own project and device names. Nothing was edited.

Not a live capture: the app requires an account, so no unauthenticated session was possible.

files.shows: One clip open in the editor: the editable transcript with word-level timing chips on the left, the 9:16 preview with a caption line, Save changes and Export in the top bar, the right tool rail (B-roll, Hook, Transitions, Text, Graphics, Audio), and the timeline with b-roll track, filmstrip and waveform.

The right rail is visible but no caption or style panel is open in this frame; the only full-window caption-panel shots the vendor publishes are animated GIFs, so this clean PNG was preferred over an extracted, palette-compressed GIF frame. Source PNG is 2926x1654; downscaled to 1424x805 and centred on the 1440x900 canvas. Not a live capture.

files.shows: The publish and download step on one generated clip: the clip detail page with its preview, virality breakdown and scene analysis, beside the action column with Publish on Social, Export XML, Download 4K, Download HD, Retry, Edit clip and AI hook.
files.note: Full-window vendor shot of the real app, published in Opus Clip's own help centre. Carries the help centre's callout bubble over Publish on Social. The window itself sits centred in a large empty dark field in the original, which the canvas preserves. Source PNG is 2828x1414; downscaled to 1424x712 and centred on the 1440x900 canvas. Not a live capture.

files.shows: CapCut desktop Home: left rail with Home, Templates, Spaces and AI design, the Create project banner, the AI tool cards, and the Projects grid of recent projects with durations and sizes.
files.note: Full-window vendor shot, not a live capture. Downloaded from CapCut's own site; the 2700x1744 PNG was scaled down to fit 1440x900 and centred on a neutral canvas, never stretched. The vendor itself blurred the account chip; nothing else was edited.

files.note: Full-window vendor shot, not a live capture. Source 1388x734 PNG composited at 1:1, with no upscaling, centred on a neutral canvas. It shows the in-app import surface, not the operating system's file picker.

files.shows: CapCut desktop export dialog over a project: cover preview, Name and Export to fields, Video section with the Resolution menu open (480P through 8K), plus bit rate, codec, format, frame rate, size estimate and the Export, Export in ultra HD and Cancel buttons.
files.note: Full-window vendor shot, not a live capture. Source 1723x955 PNG downscaled to 1440 wide with ffmpeg and centred on a neutral canvas. Shows the export dialog with its resolution menu open; no annotation overlays.

files.shows: The issues list in dark theme: the workspace sidebar (Inbox, My issues, Workspace, Projects, Views, More, Your teams), the Engineering team's Active issues tab strip, Filter and Display controls, the 'In Review 12' group and its rows with status, priority, labels, assignee and dates.
files.note: Vendor screenshot of the real app, not a live capture, and not a 1440x900 window: the vendor published it at 2820x1352 with a docs-page gradient behind the window. Trimmed to the window's own bounds to drop the backdrop, then downscaled to 1440 wide (1440x744) and centred on #111111. The vendor cut the window at the bottom, so the list runs past the frame.

files.shows: An issue detail in light theme: team breadcrumb and title 'Fix memory leak in map view controller', the description, the add-sub-issue and links rows, Activity with a generated Discussion summary, and the right-hand Properties panel holding status Done, priority Urgent, assignee, Labels, Cycle and Project.
files.note: Vendor screenshot of the real app, not a live capture. Cropped surface: the asset is the issue panel alone, with no app sidebar or tab strip. Scaled from 1682x1465 down to 1033x900 to fit the canvas height, centred on #111111, never upscaled or stretched. The vendor's crop ends mid-activity.

files.shows: The new-issue composer in dark theme: team and template breadcrumb, the title and a description with an @mention, the Bug and Design suggestion pills, the property row (Backlog, Medium, assignee, Project), and a footer with attach, Create more and the primary Create issue button.
files.note: Vendor screenshot of the real app, not a live capture. Cropped surface, composited at 1:1: its native 1224x534 with 4 px of page border trimmed to 1214x524, centred on #111111. Deliberately not upscaled, so it reads smaller than the canvas rather than softer.

files.shows: A shipped release: the 1.65.0 tab, '47 issues' all under a Done group, every row carrying its pull request and assignee, and the release sidebar reading Released, Mar 16, with per-assignee counts. This is Linear's closest surface to a finished set.
files.note: Vendor screenshot of the real app, not a live capture. Downscaled from 2234x1002 to 1440 wide (1440x646) and centred on #111111. Keeps the docs page's blurred backdrop and the vendor's cut at the right edge; not a clean window capture.

files.shows: Drive view: left sidebar (Enterprise Drive, Home, Recents, Shared with me, Workspaces, Tools), the Personal workspace header with Record and New project, a grid/list toggle, and a table of video items with thumbnails, name, duration, created and last-viewed columns. A right-click context menu (Clear local cache, Rename, Duplicate, Move to, Copy link, Access, Delete) is open over the last column.
files.note: Full-window vendor capture of the real app, 3024x1656 at source, downscaled to 1440 wide and centred on a neutral canvas; the bars above and below are the canvas, not the app. Descript publishes no screenshot of a dedicated generated-clips list, so this is its closest listing surface: the Drive table of video items with durations and dates. The source is 1.83:1, wider than 1440x900, so it was fitted by height rather than cropped, to keep the sidebar and every column.

panel.note: The files named <product>-<state>@1440.png are the panel reference set: real product UI, unlabeled and shuffled when judges see it. Each entry records whether it is a live capture, a vendor full-window screenshot, or a cropped surface composited on a 1440x900 canvas.
